- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- humanize-ai-writing: Force any writing to follow human patterns and strip every known sign of AI-generated text ("AI slop"). Use whenever producing or editing prose that will be read by a person, articles, blog posts, emails, captions, essays, documentation, social copy, reports, and whenever the user says "humanize this", "make it sound human", "remove AI slop", "doesn't sound like AI", "sounds robotic", or "rewrite this naturally". Apply this as a mandatory final pass on any long-form prose before delivering it.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Commands:
  list     List all sessions across all worktrees
  info     Show detailed information for a specific session
  tokens   Show token usage and optimization recommendations
  stop     Stop one or more active sessions
  current  Show the active session for the current worktree
  attach   Attach an existing agent session
  adopt    Adopt an active session from another worktree
  resume   Switch to a branch and resume its session

Examples:
  entire session list                      List all sessions
  entire session info <session-id>         Show session details
  entire session info <session-id> --json  Output as JSON
  entire session tokens <session-id>       Show token usage
  entire session stop                      Interactive stop
  entire session current                   Active session for cwd
  entire session attach <session-id>       Attach an external session
  entire session adopt <session-id> --from ../repo  Adopt a moved session
  entire session resume <branch>           Resume from a branch

Usage:
  entire session [command]

Aliases:
  session, sessions

Available Commands:
=== EXPLAIN ===
Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID

```
entire checkpoint list --no-pager
```

That's the one — the quoted line on each checkpoint *is* the originating prompt (truncated to ~55 chars in the human view).

Two things worth knowing:

- **Full, untruncated prompts:** `entire checkpoint explain <id>` — e.g. `entire checkpoint explain a65a3b405513`. The `--json` output on `list` does *not* carry the prompt; it only has `message` (the commit message), so `explain` is the way to get the whole text.
- **Scope:** `list` covers the current branch only. For everything across branches/worktrees use `entire session list`, or `entire search "<text>"` to grep prompts semantically.

content.content:
# Entire Enable Checklist

Run through this on **your own machine** before the hackathon. Git hooks live in
`.git/hooks` and are never shared through git, so every teammate does this individually.
See [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) for the full explanation.

## One-time enable

- [ ] `git pull` **first** — get the shared config before creating any local config
- [ ] `brew tap entireio/tap && brew trust entireio/tap && brew install --cask entire`
- [ ] `entire enable --agent claude-code`
- [ ] `entire doctor` — all four checks green:
      Metadata branches / Git hooks / Claude Code hook config / no stuck sessions
- [ ] `entire status` — shows `● Enabled`, your branch, `Agents · Claude Code`

## Verify capture actually works

Enabling is not the same as capturing. `entire doctor` can be all-green while nothing
is being recorded. Confirm all three:

- [ ] **Launch Claude Code from the repo root.** `cd` into the repo *before* starting the
      session. The hooks live in the repo's `.claude/settings.json`, so a session rooted in
      a parent directory never loads them and captures nothing.
- [ ] **Start a NEW session after enabling.** Hooks are read at session start, so a session
      already running when you ran `entire enable` will never be captured.
- [ ] **Make the session modify a file.** Read-only or chat-only sessions are skipped by
      design — the log says `no files modified during session, skipping checkpoint`.
- [ ] Then `entire checkpoint list` — your prompt text should appear as a checkpoint row
- [ ] `git push`, then `git ls-remote origin | grep entire` — you should see BOTH
      `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1` and a `refs/entire/checkpoints/...` payload ref

## What does and does not create a checkpoint

A checkpoint needs **all three** of: a session rooted in this repo, started after enable,
that actually changed files.

- Creates a checkpoint: an agent session in the repo that edits/writes files
- Creates **nothing**: hand-typed `git commit`; a session started from a parent directory;
  a session that only read files or answered questions; a session predating `entire enable`

So a repo full of manual commits — or a session you ran from one directory up — shows zero
checkpoints while `entire doctor` reports perfect health. Trust `entire checkpoint list`,
not `doctor`.

## Seeing each other's checkpoints across devices

Two separate things have to be true. Getting one right does nothing for the other.

**1. Capture — per person, every session.** Launch Claude Code with *this repo* as the
working directory:

```bash
cd /path/to/ehl-bayern-codewerk   # NOT the parent folder
claude
```

The hooks come from this repo's `.claude/settings.json`. A session rooted one directory up
loads no hooks and records nothing, however much it edits. Verify with `entire checkpoint list`
after a session that changed files.

**2. Visibility — once per clone, on every machine.** Pushing works out of the box (the
pre-push hook syncs checkpoints), but *fetching* does not. Checkpoint payloads live in the
`refs/entire/*` namespace, and git's default refspec only fetches `refs/heads/*` — so you
never pull down a teammate's checkpoints. Fix it once per clone:

```bash
git config --add remote.origin.fetch '+refs/entire/*:refs/entire/*'
git fetch origin
```

This is local git config, so it is **not** shared through the repo — every teammate runs it
on every machine they clone to. Confirm it worked:

```bash
git ls-remote origin | grep entire            # what the remote holds
git for-each-ref | grep refs/entire           # what you now hold locally
```

Note `entire checkpoint list` can still show a checkpoint from local `.entire/metadata/`
even when the ref is missing, so on a fresh clone trust the ref listing, not the count.

## Submission-gate risk — UNRESOLVED, ask Entire staff on site

EHL can require the submitted repo to carry `entire/checkpoints/v1` with at least one
captured prompt, and submitted repos are **auto-forked** to a snapshot org.

In this repo the payload lives at `refs/entire/checkpoints/<...>` — a custom ref
namespace. The branch `entire/checkpoints/v1` itself is an empty init commit with no
files in its tree. GitHub forks copy `refs/heads` and `refs/tags` only, **not** custom
namespaces, so the payload may not survive the fork.

- [ ] Test it: throwaway public repo → `entire enable` → one real session → push →
      fork on GitHub → confirm a captured prompt is still visible in the fork
- [ ] Ask Entire (tech partner, on site) how the gate reads checkpoints from a fork

## If `git pull` fails with "untracked working tree files would be overwritten"

You ran `entire enable` before pulling. One-time fix:

```bash
rm -f .claude/settings.json .entire/.gitignore .entire/settings.json
git pull
```

## Daily

- [ ] `git pull` before starting work
- [ ] `git push` after finishing — the pre-push hook syncs checkpoints alongside your commits

# ehl-bayern-codewerk
We, Team Bayern CodeWerk use this repository for collaborating for the EHL Hackathon in Munich.

See [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) for one-time Entire CLI checkpoint tracking setup.
=========== SETUP ===========
# Team Setup: Entire CLI Checkpoint Tracking

This repo tracks AI coding session checkpoints with the [Entire CLI](https://entire.io),
which EHL sponsors may require for submission (`entire/checkpoints/v1` branch).

Checkpoint config (`.entire/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.entire/.gitignore`)
is already committed to `main` so everyone shares the same setup. To avoid local file
conflicts, follow this order exactly:

## One-time setup (do this first, before anything else)

1. **Pull the repo first** — get the shared config before creating any local config of your own:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hxrshx/ehl-bayern-codewerk.git
   cd ehl-bayern-codewerk
   ```
   (If you already cloned earlier, just run `git pull`.)

2. **Install the Entire CLI:**
   ```bash
   brew tap entireio/tap
   brew trust entireio/tap
   brew install --cask entire
   ```

3. **Enable tracking for Claude Code** (reads the already-committed config, just installs
   your local git hooks — hooks live in `.git/hooks` and are never shared via git, so
   everyone must run this individually):
   ```bash
   entire enable --agent claude-code
   ```

4. Verify it worked:
   ```bash
   entire doctor
   entire status
   ```

## Daily workflow

```bash
git pull    # before starting work — pick up teammates' checkpoints
...work...
git push    # after finishing — share your checkpoints
```

## If `git pull` fails with "untracked working tree files would be overwritten"

This means you ran `entire enable` before pulling, so you have local copies of the
same config files that are now conflicting with the committed ones. Fix once:

```bash
rm -f .claude/settings.json .entire/.gitignore .entire/settings.json
git pull
```

After this one-time fix, future pulls work normally.

## Checking checkpoints

```bash
entire session list      # sessions tracked on this machine
entire checkpoint list   # checkpoints on the current branch
entire status            # overall health + active sessions
```

  dispatch                   Generate a dispatch summarizing recent agent work
  recap                      Summarize recent checkpoint activity

> "Entire is a CLI-first system of record that captures the context behind agent-assisted code changes and links it to Git."

**Why Entire Exists** — when an agent changes code, the final diff leaves out:
- The prompt that started the work
- Files the agent inspected
- Tools it ran
- Decisions it made
- Checkpoints it created along the way (links to `/guides/checkpoints/overview`)

"Entire records that context so teams can review, search, and continue agent work with the same confidence they expect from Git history."

**What Entire Helps You Do**
- Review the prompt, transcript, and tool calls behind a commit, not just the diff.
- Browse Checkpoints from an agent session as the work evolves.
- Search prompts, sessions, and repository history.
- Continue from prior agent work instead of starting cold.
- Share agent context with teammates through Git-linked history.

**How It Works** (numbered, verbatim)
1. Install the Entire CLI in your repository.
2. Connect Entire to the coding agent you use.
3. Entire captures sessions and Checkpoints as the agent works.
4. Use the CLI or Entire.io to inspect the history behind commits.

Core concepts named on `/index.md` (one-line descriptions only, each linking elsewhere):
- **Checkpoints** — "Versioned records of agent-assisted changes." (`/guides/checkpoints/overview`)

- **Sessions** — "The prompts and tool calls behind a run." (`/guides/sessions/overview`)
- **Search** — "Find past sessions, commits, prompts, files, and reasoning." (`/guides/search/overview`)

## 2. Installation

### System requirements (`/installation.md` only)
- **Operating System:** macOS, Linux, Windows
- **Git:** Version 2.25 or later
- **Shell:** Bash or Zsh (for hook installation)

Quickstart's prerequisites are looser and differently worded:
- Git installed and configured
- An AI coding agent installed, such as Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Factory, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, or Pi
- macOS, Linux, or Windows
- Optional: GitHub CLI (`gh`) installed and authenticated, if you want Entire to create and push a private GitHub repository during setup

### Release channels
Stated identically on `/installation.md` and `/updating.md`:
- `stable`: recommended for most users. **This is the default channel for Homebrew, Scoop, and `install.sh`.**
- `nightly`: prerelease builds for users who want the latest changes earlier.

Quickstart adds: "Nightly is available through Homebrew and the Linux install script. Scoop currently supports stable only."

Installation notes: "Entire uses Homebrew casks so the CLI can be installed from the same signed release artifacts used by other install methods."

### macOS — Homebrew
One-time tap + trust:
```bash
brew tap entireio/tap
brew trust entireio/tap
```
> **Note (installation.md):** "Homebrew 5.2.0 and 6.0.0 and later require trusting a third-party tap with `brew trust` before installing its casks." Links to https://docs.brew.sh/Tap-Trust

Install stable:
```bash
brew install --cask entire
```
Install nightly:
```bash
brew install --cask entire@nightly
```
Upgrade:
```bash
brew upgrade --cask entire
```
```bash
brew upgrade --cask entire@nightly
```

### Linux — install script
Stable is the default:
```bash
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
```
Nightly:
```bash
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
```

### Linux — direct binary download (installation.md only)
```bash
# Download the latest release
curl -LO https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/latest/download/entire-linux-amd64.tar.gz

# Extract and install
tar -xzf entire-linux-amd64.tar.gz
sudo mv entire /usr/local/bin/
```
For ARM64 systems:
```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/latest/download/entire-linux-arm64.tar.gz
```
*(The docs give the ARM64 download line only — no separate extract/move lines are shown for ARM64.)*

### Windows — Scoop
"Scoop currently supports the stable channel only:"
```bash
scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
scoop install entire/cli
```
Update:
```bash
scoop update entire/cli
```

### From source
Requires Go 1.21+:
```bash
go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest
```
Or clone and build manually:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/entireio/cli.git
cd cli
go build -o entire ./cmd/entire
sudo mv entire /usr/local/bin/
```
`/updating.md` classifies source as: "manual/development flow, not a managed release channel."

### Verify installation
```bash
entire version
```
Expected output shape:
```
entire version 1.0.0 (abc1234)
```
> "The `entire` binary needs to be on your `$PATH` for agent hooks and Git hooks to work."

### Shell completion
Bash — add to `~/.bashrc`:
```bash
source <(entire completion bash)
```
Zsh — add to `~/.zshrc`:
```bash
source <(entire completion zsh)
```
*(Only Bash and Zsh are documented. No fish/PowerShell completion is mentioned anywhere.)*

### Uninstalling
Homebrew:
```bash
brew uninstall --cask entire
```
Manual:


```bash
rm -rf ~/.config/entire
```

## 4. Quickstart, in order (`/quickstart.md`)

Framing: "This quickstart walks you from installing Entire to creating your first checkpoint: a record of the prompts, transcript, tool calls, and file changes behind an AI-assisted commit."

**Step 1 — Install Entire.** Same four tabs as the installation page (Homebrew stable/nightly, Linux script stable/nightly, Scoop, source). Homebrew tab is annotated `# One-time setup: tap and trust`. Then verify with `entire version`.

**Step 2 — Create a Demo Project**
```bash
mkdir entire-demo
cd entire-demo
```
> **Note:** "Already in a Git repository? Skip this step and run the remaining commands from the repository root."

**Step 3 — Enable Entire.** "Choose the agent you already use, then run its setup command."

| Agent | Command |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `entire enable -y --agent claude-code` |
| Codex | `entire enable -y --agent codex` |
| Copilot CLI | `entire enable -y --agent copilot-cli` |
| Cursor | `entire enable -y --agent cursor` |
| Factory | `entire enable -y --agent factoryai-droid` |
| Gemini CLI | `entire enable -y --agent gemini` |
| OpenCode | `entire enable -y --agent opencode` |
| Pi | `entire enable -y --agent pi` |

What it does, verbatim: "This installs Git hooks that capture checkpoints when you commit and installs hook configuration for your selected agent. It also creates a `.entire/` directory for project and local settings."

Config file guidance: "For shared projects, commit `.entire/settings.json` and `.entire/.gitignore`. Keep `.entire/settings.local.json` local for personal overrides."

> **Note:** "Because this starts in a new folder, `entire enable -y` initializes Git and creates an initial commit. If `gh` is installed and authenticated, Entire can also create a private GitHub repository and push the initial commit."

**Step 4 — Start an Agent Session.** Launch commands per agent: `claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `droid` (Factory), `gemini`, `opencode`, `pi`.

Suggested prompt (verbatim text block):
```text
Create a file named hello-entire.md with a short note explaining that this repo is my first Entire checkpoint demo.
```
"When the agent finishes, exit the agent session if needed."

**Step 5 — Commit the Change**
```bash
git status
```
```bash
git add hello-entire.md
git commit -m "Add first Entire demo file"
```
"Because Entire detected recent agent work, it may ask whether to link this commit to the session context. The agent name will match the integration you enabled:"
```text
Entire: Active <agent> session detected
  Last prompt: Create a file named hello-entire.md with a short note...

Link this commit to session context?
  [Y]es / [n]o / [a]lways (remember my choice):
```
"Press `Enter` or type `y` to link the commit. After the commit succeeds, you have created your first checkpoint."
> **Note:** "If you choose `always`, Entire remembers that preference and links future matching commits automatically."

**Step 6 — View Your First Checkpoint**
```bash
entire checkpoint list
```
"You should see the checkpoint linked to your commit."

Storage branch — "Entire stores permanent checkpoint data on a Git branch named:"
```text
entire/checkpoints/v1
```
"Your working branch stays clean. Entire does not add extra commits to it."

**Step 7 (Optional) — Push Your Code and Checkpoint**
```bash
git push
```
"Entire's pre-push hook also syncs checkpoint data to `entire/checkpoints/v1`."

> **Privacy note (important):** "Checkpoint data can include session context. If your repository is public, pushed checkpoint history is public too." Links: `/security`, `/guides/configuration/checkpoint-storage#checkpoint-remote`.

## 5. CLI vs Entire.io

`/platforms/overview.md`: "Entire has two main surfaces: the CLI and Entire.io."

- CLI: "runs locally in your development environment. It captures agent sessions, creates checkpoints, connects work to Git commits, and gives agents a way to search, review, and reuse prior context."
- Entire.io: "the web app for reviewing and sharing that history. Use it to browse repositories, inspect checkpoints and sessions, search past work, and understand what happened across a team."
- "Most workflows use both. The CLI records the work as it happens. Entire.io makes that work easier to review, search, and collaborate on."

### The CLI (`/platforms/cli.md`)
"The Entire CLI is the local capture and automation layer for Entire. It runs in your Git repository, installs the hooks needed to observe supported agents, and records the context behind agent-assisted development. When you commit, the CLI connects that captured context to Git so future reviewers and agents can understand why the code changed."

"Use the CLI when you are setting up Entire, working from a terminal, scripting a workflow, or giving an agent access to Entire history."

**What the CLI Does** (verbatim bullets):
- Enables Entire in a local repository.
- Captures agent sessions as you work.
- Creates checkpoints and links them to commits.
- Searches prior checkpoints, sessions, and commits.
- Generates dispatches from repository history.
- Manages repository mirrors from the terminal.
- Provides JSON output for automation and agent workflows.

*Thin-page flag:* `/platforms/cli.md` contains **no commands or flags at all** — it defers everything to `/cli-reference`, `/guides/checkpoints/review-in-cli`, `/guides/search/search-in-cli`, `/guides/dispatches/dispatches-in-cli`.

### Entire.io (`/platforms/entire-io.md`)
"Entire.io is the web app for reviewing, searching, and sharing the history captured by Entire."

"Use Entire.io when you want a visual way to understand agent work: what changed, which prompt or session produced it, how a checkpoint relates to a commit, and what happened across a repository or team."

Explicit boundary: "**Entire.io does not replace the CLI. The CLI captures the work locally. Entire.io helps you browse and collaborate on that captured history.**"

**What Entire.io Is For** (verbatim bullets):
- Browse repositories connected to Entire.
- Review checkpoints by repository and branch.
- Inspect the sessions behind a checkpoint.
- Search checkpoints, sessions, and commits visually.
- Review dispatches and share summarized work.
- Understand agent activity without reconstructing it from Git alone.

**Activity Overview:** "After you sign in, Entire.io shows activity across connected repositories, including recent commits, repository activity, and captured checkpoint history." (Accompanied by a hero walkthrough video and a dashboard screenshot; no sign-up/pricing/auth instructions appear anywhere.)

### Capability split as documented

| Capability | CLI | Entire.io |
|---|---|---|
| Enable Entire in a repo / install hooks | yes | not mentioned |
| Capture agent sessions | yes | no (capture is local) |
| Create checkpoints, link to commits | yes | no |
| Review checkpoints | yes (`review-in-cli`) | yes, "visually", by repository and branch |
| Inspect sessions | yes | yes |
| Search checkpoints/sessions/commits | yes | yes, "visually", open results in context |
| Dispatches | generate from repository history | create, review, and share summaries |
| Repository mirrors | yes ("Manages repository mirrors from the terminal") | not mentioned |
| JSON output for automation | yes | n/a |
| Configure storage | listed on `/index.md` card ("configure storage") | not mentioned |
| Share context with team | via Git-linked history | yes, explicit |

Small wording difference worth knowing (not a contradiction): `/index.md`'s CLI card says "Capture sessions, create Checkpoints, configure storage, and automate workflows," while `/platforms/cli.md`'s own bullet list omits "configure storage" and adds mirrors + JSON output. Likewise `/platforms/overview.md`'s CLI card mentions "generate dispatches" and "inspect sessions," and its Entire.io card mentions "create dispatches" — whereas `/platforms/entire-io.md` says "Review dispatches and share summarized work" (review vs create). Treat "create dispatches in Entire.io" as stated only on the overview card.

## 4. Quickstart, in order (`/quickstart.md`)

Framing: "This quickstart walks you from installing Entire to creating your first checkpoint: a record of the prompts, transcript, tool calls, and file changes behind an AI-assisted commit."

**Step 1 — Install Entire.** Same four tabs as the installation page (Homebrew stable/nightly, Linux script stable/nightly, Scoop, source). Homebrew tab is annotated `# One-time setup: tap and trust`. Then verify with `entire version`.

**Step 2 — Create a Demo Project**
```bash
mkdir entire-demo
cd entire-demo
```
> **Note:** "Already in a Git repository? Skip this step and run the remaining commands from the repository root."

**Step 3 — Enable Entire.** "Choose the agent you already use, then run its setup command."

| Agent | Command |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `entire enable -y --agent claude-code` |
| Codex | `entire enable -y --agent codex` |
| Copilot CLI | `entire enable -y --agent copilot-cli` |
| Cursor | `entire enable -y --agent cursor` |
| Factory | `entire enable -y --agent factoryai-droid` |
| Gemini CLI | `entire enable -y --agent gemini` |
| OpenCode | `entire enable -y --agent opencode` |
| Pi | `entire enable -y --agent pi` |

What it does, verbatim: "This installs Git hooks that capture checkpoints when you commit and installs hook configuration for your selected agent. It also creates a `.entire/` directory for project and local settings."

Config file guidance: "For shared projects, commit `.entire/settings.json` and `.entire/.gitignore`. Keep `.entire/settings.local.json` local for personal overrides."

> **Note:** "Because this starts in a new folder, `entire enable -y` initializes Git and creates an initial commit. If `gh` is installed and authenticated, Entire can also create a private GitHub repository and push the initial commit."

**Step 4 — Start an Agent Session.** Launch commands per agent: `claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `droid` (Factory), `gemini`, `opencode`, `pi`.

Suggested prompt (verbatim text block):
```text
Create a file named hello-entire.md with a short note explaining that this repo is my first Entire checkpoint demo.
```
"When the agent finishes, exit the agent session if needed."

**Step 5 — Commit the Change**
```bash
git status
```
```bash
git add hello-entire.md
git commit -m "Add first Entire demo file"
```
"Because Entire detected recent agent work, it may ask whether to link this commit to the session context. The agent name will match the integration you enabled:"
```text
Entire: Active <agent> session detected
  Last prompt: Create a file named hello-entire.md with a short note...

Link this commit to session context?
  [Y]es / [n]o / [a]lways (remember my choice):
```
"Press `Enter` or type `y` to link the commit. After the commit succeeds, you have created your first checkpoint."
> **Note:** "If you choose `always`, Entire remembers that preference and links future matching commits automatically."

**Step 6 — View Your First Checkpoint**
```bash
entire checkpoint list
```
"You should see the checkpoint linked to your commit."

Storage branch — "Entire stores permanent checkpoint data on a Git branch named:"
```text
entire/checkpoints/v1
```
"Your working branch stays clean. Entire does not add extra commits to it."

**Step 7 (Optional) — Push Your Code and Checkpoint**
```bash
git push
```
"Entire's pre-push hook also syncs checkpoint data to `entire/checkpoints/v1`."

> **Privacy note (important):** "Checkpoint data can include session context. If your repository is public, pushed checkpoint history is public too." Links: `/security`, `/guides/configuration/checkpoint-storage#checkpoint-remote`.

## 5. CLI vs Entire.io

`/platforms/overview.md`: "Entire has two main surfaces: the CLI and Entire.io."

- CLI: "runs locally in your development environment. It captures agent sessions, creates checkpoints, connects work to Git commits, and gives agents a way to search, review, and reuse prior context."
- Entire.io: "the web app for reviewing and sharing that history. Use it to browse repositories, inspect checkpoints and sessions, search past work, and understand what happened across a team."
- "Most workflows use both. The CLI records the work as it happens. Entire.io makes that work easier to review, search, and collaborate on."

### The CLI (`/platforms/cli.md`)
"The Entire CLI is the local capture and automation layer for Entire. It runs in your Git repository, installs the hooks needed to observe supported agents, and records the context behind agent-assisted development. When you commit, the CLI connects that captured context to Git so future reviewers and agents can understand why the code changed."

"Use the CLI when you are setting up Entire, working from a terminal, scripting a workflow, or giving an agent access to Entire history."

**What the CLI Does** (verbatim bullets):
- Enables Entire in a local repository.
- Captures agent sessions as you work.
- Creates checkpoints and links them to commits.
- Searches prior checkpoints, sessions, and commits.
- Generates dispatches from repository history.
- Manages repository mirrors from the terminal.
- Provides JSON output for automation and agent workflows.

*Thin-page flag:* `/platforms/cli.md` contains **no commands or flags at all** — it defers everything to `/cli-reference`, `/guides/checkpoints/review-in-cli`, `/guides/search/search-in-cli`, `/guides/dispatches/dispatches-in-cli`.

### Entire.io (`/platforms/entire-io.md`)
"Entire.io is the web app for reviewing, searching, and sharing the history captured by Entire."

"Use Entire.io when you want a visual way to understand agent work: what changed, which prompt or session produced it, how a checkpoint relates to a commit, and what happened across a repository or team."

Explicit boundary: "**Entire.io does not replace the CLI. The CLI captures the work locally. Entire.io helps you browse and collaborate on that captured history.**"

**What Entire.io Is For** (verbatim bullets):
- Browse repositories connected to Entire.
- Review checkpoints by repository and branch.
- Inspect the sessions behind a checkpoint.
- Search checkpoints, sessions, and commits visually.
- Review dispatches and share summarized work.
- Understand agent activity without reconstructing it from Git alone.

**Activity Overview:** "After you sign in, Entire.io shows activity across connected repositories, including recent commits, repository activity, and captured checkpoint history." (Accompanied by a hero walkthrough video and a dashboard screenshot; no sign-up/pricing/auth instructions appear anywhere.)

### Capability split as documented

| Capability | CLI | Entire.io |
|---|---|---|
| Enable Entire in a repo / install hooks | yes | not mentioned |
| Capture agent sessions | yes | no (capture is local) |
| Create checkpoints, link to commits | yes | no |
| Review checkpoints | yes (`review-in-cli`) | yes, "visually", by repository and branch |
| Inspect sessions | yes | yes |
| Search checkpoints/sessions/commits | yes | yes, "visually", open results in context |
| Dispatches | generate from repository history | create, review, and share summaries |
| Repository mirrors | yes ("Manages repository mirrors from the terminal") | not mentioned |
| JSON output for automation | yes | n/a |
| Configure storage | listed on `/index.md` card ("configure storage") | not mentioned |
| Share context with team | via Git-linked history | yes, explicit |

Small wording difference worth knowing (not a contradiction): `/index.md`'s CLI card says "Capture sessions, create Checkpoints, configure storage, and automate workflows," while `/platforms/cli.md`'s own bullet list omits "configure storage" and adds mirrors + JSON output. Likewise `/platforms/overview.md`'s CLI card mentions "generate dispatches" and "inspect sessions," and its Entire.io card mentions "create dispatches" — whereas `/platforms/entire-io.md` says "Review dispatches and share summarized work" (review vs create). Treat "create dispatches in Entire.io" as stated only on the overview card.

## 2. Full settings schema

### 2.1 Precedence (from `overview.md`, verbatim)

> Entire merges settings from multiple places. More specific settings win:
> 1. Local settings: `.entire/settings.local.json`
> 2. Project settings: `.entire/settings.json`
> 3. Global settings: `~/.config/entire/settings.json`
> 4. Defaults

Guidance: "Use project settings for behavior the whole team should share. Use local settings for personal preferences, machine-specific setup, debug logging, or private redaction rules."

Merging is partial, not wholesale replacement: "Local settings are merged with project settings. You only need to specify the settings you want to override."

One documented exception to file-based precedence: `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL` "takes precedence over settings files."

### 2.2 Project settings schema — `.entire/settings.json` (verbatim table with defaults)

Initial file created by Entire:

```json
{
  "enabled": true
}
```

| Setting path | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Whether Entire is active in this repository |
| `commit_linking` | string | `"prompt"` | Controls whether Entire prompts before linking a Git commit to recent agent session context |
| `strategy_options.push_sessions` | boolean | `true` | Automatically push checkpoint data when someone runs `git push` |
| `strategy_options.checkpoint_remote` | object | `null` | Push checkpoint data to a separate repository |
| `strategy_options.summarize.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Auto-generate checkpoint summaries at commit time |
| `redaction.pii.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Enable optional PII redaction on top of always-on secret redaction |
| `redaction.custom_redactions` | object | `{}` | Add shared regex rules that replace matches with `REDACTED` |
| `telemetry` | boolean/null | `null` | Send anonymous usage analytics for this repository |
| `sign_checkpoint_commits` | boolean | `true` | Sign checkpoint commits using your existing Git signing key |
| `log_level` | string | `"info"` | Log verbosity: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` |
| `external_agents` | boolean | `false` | Enable discovery of external agent plugins from `$PATH` |
| `absolute_git_hook_path` | boolean | `false` | Embed the full `entire` binary path in Git hooks for GUI Git clients |

Plus, from `review-profiles.md`:

| Setting path | Type | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `review_default_profile` | string | The default review profile name |
| `review_profiles` | object | Named review profiles and their reviewer, judge, output, task, model, and slot settings |

**NOT IN DOCS:** the allowed values of `commit_linking` beyond the default `"prompt"`; the inner schema of `review_profiles`. On the latter the docs say only: "The profile JSON can contain nested reviewer and model settings, so the CLI is the safest way to keep the shape valid."

### 2.3 Local settings — `.entire/settings.local.json`

"Local settings have the highest priority and are used for personal preferences, private rules, machine-specific paths, and temporary debugging."

Example given:

```json
{
  "log_level": "debug",
  "telemetry": false
}
```

The local-settings reference table lists the same paths *minus* `enabled` and `strategy_options.summarize.enabled`: `commit_linking`, `strategy_options.push_sessions`, `strategy_options.checkpoint_remote`, `redaction.pii.enabled`, `redaction.custom_redactions`, `telemetry`, `sign_checkpoint_commits`, `log_level`, `external_agents`, `absolute_git_hook_path`. (Local review profiles are also supported per `review-profiles.md`.) No defaults column is given for the local table.

Nesting rule, verbatim: "Top-level settings are written directly" / "Dotted setting paths are written as nested objects":

```json

  "redaction": {
    "custom_redactions": {
      "private_codename": "PROJECT_[A-Z]{4}"
    }
  }
}
```

## 5. Privacy and redaction

### Always-on baseline

> By default, Entire redacts common secrets such as API keys, access tokens, credentialed URLs, database connection strings, and private keys before checkpoint metadata is stored.

### PII redaction (opt-in, default off)

Project:

```json
{
  "redaction": {
    "pii": {
      "enabled": true,
      "email": true,
      "phone": true,
      "address": false
    }
  }
}
```

Local:

```json

  "redaction": {
    "pii": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

Note the sub-keys `email`, `phone`, `address` appear only in the project example; the settings tables list just `redaction.pii.enabled`. Their defaults are **NOT IN DOCS** on this page — deferred to `/security#pii-redaction-optional` for "categories, defaults, and limitations."

### User-defined redaction

Inline rules (map of rule name → regex; matches replaced with `REDACTED` per the settings table):

```json
{
  "redaction": {

}
```

## 6. Logging and diagnostics

Log location: "Entire writes local diagnostic logs under `.entire/logs/`." "Keep logs local unless someone asks for a specific file or bundle while troubleshooting."

`log_level`: default `info`; supported values `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`.

Three ways to set it, in precedence order:

```bash
ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug entire status
```
> `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL` takes precedence over settings files.

```json
{
  "log_level": "debug"
}
```
(in `.entire/settings.local.json` for machine-specific, or `.entire/settings.json` "only when the whole repository should use the same log level")

Diagnostic commands, verbatim:

```bash
entire status --detailed     # inspect active settings; shows which settings file supplied a value
entire doctor                # repository health check
entire doctor logs           # show recent operational logs
entire doctor logs --follow  # stream new log lines
entire doctor bundle         # create diagnostic bundle
entire doctor trace          # hook performance trace
```

- `entire status --detailed` — "confirm Entire is reading the value you changed and to see which settings file supplied it." This is the verification command recommended on every single page.
- `entire doctor` — "when sessions look stuck, Git hooks are not firing, checkpoint data is not syncing, or `entire status` shows warnings. It checks repository setup, hook state, checkpoint metadata, and common session problems."
- `entire doctor bundle` — "Diagnostic bundles are redacted by default. Use `--raw` only when support has asked for an unredacted bundle."
- `entire doctor trace` — "Hook performance traces are only available at debug log level. Turn on debug logging, reproduce the slow Git command, then run `entire doctor trace`."

Documented environment variables across all nine pages: exactly two — `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL` and `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT`.

## 2. Full settings schema

### 2.1 Precedence (from `overview.md`, verbatim)

> Entire merges settings from multiple places. More specific settings win:
> 1. Local settings: `.entire/settings.local.json`
> 2. Project settings: `.entire/settings.json`
> 3. Global settings: `~/.config/entire/settings.json`
> 4. Defaults

Guidance: "Use project settings for behavior the whole team should share. Use local settings for personal preferences, machine-specific setup, debug logging, or private redaction rules."

## 1. Session vs. Checkpoint, and lifecycle

### Session — definition (verbatim, overview.md)

> A session is the complete record of an AI coding interaction: the prompts, responses, tool calls, file changes, metadata, token usage, and checkpoint links Entire captured while the agent worked.

> Sessions show what the agent did, why it did it, and how the work came together.

**What sessions capture** (overview.md, verbatim list):
- prompts and agent responses
- tool calls, shell commands, file reads, and file edits
- files created, modified, or deleted during the session
- agent, model, worktree, timing, and token metadata
- checkpoints and commits linked to the session
- line attribution showing how much of a change came from the agent versus a human

### Checkpoint — definition `[REF glossary.md]`

> **Checkpoint**: A save point for your work. Entire creates checkpoints around agent activity and links committed checkpoints to Git commits.

> **Committed checkpoint**: A checkpoint permanently linked to a Git commit and stored on the checkpoints branch.

> **Checkpoint linking**: The connection between a Git commit and the Entire checkpoint that captured the session context behind it.

> **Session** (glossary): A complete interaction with an AI coding agent from start to finish. Sessions include prompts, responses, code changes, checkpoints, token usage, metadata, and line attribution.

### Session↔Checkpoint relationship (overview.md, table verbatim)

| Scenario | How it looks in Entire |
| --- | --- |
| One session, one checkpoint | Most common. You ask the agent to do something, it does the work, and you commit. |
| One checkpoint, multiple sessions | Several sessions contribute to the same change before you commit. |
| One session, multiple checkpoints | One longer session keeps going while you commit multiple checkpoints along the way. |
| Multiple sessions, multiple checkpoints | Multiple sessions and commits are linked across a larger or parallel piece of work. |

> Entire links these records so you can move from code, to checkpoint, to the session context behind it.

### How sessions are created (overview.md, verbatim)

> After you enable Entire for a repository, agent hooks capture session context while you work. When you commit, Entire can link the relevant session context to a checkpoint.

> You can also attach a session later if capture started late, hooks did not fire, or the session was useful even though it did not produce file changes.

Also, from troubleshooting.md: "A normal committed checkpoint needs both captured session context and a Git commit."

### ⚠️ Lifecycle — what the docs actually state vs. do not

**The docs do NOT publish a formal session state machine.** No page in the sessions guide enumerates a `start → active → end → checkpoint` transition list. Do not present one as documented. What *is* documented:

- Two named phases exist, but only in `[REF doctor.md]`: **`ACTIVE`** and **`ENDED`**.
- `entire session list` shows "sessions tracked by Entire, **including ended sessions**" (list-sessions.md), implying ended is a persisted terminal state.
- `entire session stop` "**marks sessions as ended**" (stop-sessions.md warning) — this is the only documented explicit transition, and it explicitly **does not** create a checkpoint.
- Resume operates on "**stopped sessions**" (resume-sessions.md) — "stopped" is used as a session state in the picker.
- Storage transition `[REF glossary.md + doctor.md]`: **Shadow branch** = "A temporary local branch used to store checkpoints during active sessions. Shadow branches are named like `entire/<sessionID>-<worktreeID>` and are not pushed to remote repositories." **Checkpoints branch** = "The permanent Git branch where Entire stores checkpoint and session metadata. The branch is named `entire/checkpoints/v1`." `doctor`'s **Condense** action moves data from the former to the latter.
- **Nested session** `[REF glossary.md]`: "A child session created when an agent spawns another agent or sub-agent during the same body of work." Behavior (sessions-in-entire-io.md): "When an agent spawns a sub-agent, Entire can capture that child session separately and roll its context into the parent checkpoint."
- **Agent run** `[REF glossary.md]`: "One execution of an agent inside a session." So a session can contain multiple runs.

```bash
entire session stop --all --force
```

| Flag | Description `[REF]` |

### `session attach`

```bash
entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent AGENT
entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent AGENT --force
entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent codex --review

```

`[REF attach.md]` signature: `entire session attach SESSION_ID [flags]`

| Flag | Description `[REF]` |
| --- | --- |
| `-a, --agent NAME` | Agent that created the session. Defaults to `claude-code`. Run `entire agent list` to see registered agents, including external agents. |

| `--skills SKILL` | Declare which review skills were run. Repeatable; only used with `--review`. |

**When to attach** (attach-sessions.md, verbatim bullets):
- hooks were not installed when the session started
- hooks did not fire
- a research session should be linked to the latest commit
- a completed agent review should be preserved as review context

**Behavior:** "Attach reads an existing agent transcript, creates or updates a checkpoint, and links that context to the last commit. If the last commit already has an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, the session is added to that checkpoint. Otherwise, Entire creates a checkpoint and can amend the last commit with the trailer."

> **Note `[REF attach.md]`:** `entire session attach` requires the repository to already have at least one commit. If Entire cannot find the transcript for the agent you specify, it will try to auto-detect the correct agent from known transcript locations.

| --- | --- |


`[REF resume.md]` signature: `entire session resume [BRANCH] [flags]`

| Argument | Description `[REF]` |

| `branch` | Optional branch to resume the agent session from |

| Flag | Description `[REF]` |

**Branch mode — exact numbered steps `[REF resume.md]`:**
1. Checks out the specified branch
2. Finds the session ID from commits unique to this branch
3. Restores the session log if it does not exist locally
4. Shows or starts the command to resume the agent session

(Guide wording: "Entire finds the session ID from checkpoint-linked commits on that branch.")

> **Note `[REF]`:** If the branch doesn't exist locally but exists on origin, you'll be prompted to fetch it.

> **Warning (resume-sessions.md, verbatim):** If newer commits without checkpoints exist on the branch, resume can reset Git state to the most recent commit with a checkpoint. Entire prompts before doing this unless you force it.

> **Warning `[REF]`, fuller:** If newer commits without checkpoints exist on the branch (e.g., after merging main or cherry-picking), this operation will reset your Git status to the most recent commit with a checkpoint. You'll be prompted to confirm.

**When to use** (import-past-agent-history.md, verbatim bullets):
- you enabled Entire after useful agent work already happened
- you want past local agent sessions to become searchable in Entire
- you want to import sessions from an agent's local transcript store

| If you want to | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Bring past local agent sessions into Entire | `entire import AGENT` |
| Link one missed session to the latest commit | `entire session attach` |

```bash
entire import claude-code
entire import claude-code --session SESSION_ID
```

- Run import **from inside the repository** whose agent history you want to bring in.
- Replace `claude-code` with the agent you want to import from.
- `--dry-run` preview "shows how many sessions and turns Entire found, what would be imported, and what was already imported."
- "You can repeat `--session` to import more than one session."
- "Run `entire import --help` or see the import command reference for supported agents and flags."

| Flag `[REF import.md]` | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Report what would be imported without writing checkpoints |
| `--path DIRECTORY` | Override the transcript directory to import from |
| `--session ID` | Import only this session ID. Repeatable. |

| Agent | Command |

**⚠️ Experimental status `[REF import.md]`:**

> `entire import` is experimental and hidden from the top-level help in Entire CLI `0.7.8`. Run `entire import --help` to see the agents supported by your installed CLI version.

## 4. Stuck / orphaned sessions

**Terminology caveat:** the docs never use the word "orphaned." The nine guides use "**stale**"; the CLI reference uses "**stuck**." Treat them as the documented vocabulary.

### How they happen
- Guides state only the situational cause: "Stop a session when Entire still considers it active, but the agent run is finished or no longer relevant." (stop-sessions.md)
- Wrong-worktree case: "If an agent started in one worktree and continued in another…" (troubleshooting.md)

### Detection — exact criteria `[REF doctor.md]`

> A session is considered stuck if:
> * It is in ACTIVE phase with no interaction for over 1 hour
> * It is in ENDED phase with uncondensed checkpoint data on a shadow branch

Detection commands:

```bash
entire status          # find active and stale sessions
entire doctor          # scan for stuck sessions and offer fixes
```

### Clearing

```bash
entire session stop SESSION_ID
entire session stop --all
entire session stop --all --force
entire doctor
```

`entire doctor` flags and choices `[REF doctor.md]`:

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-f, --force` | Fix all issues without prompting (condense if possible, otherwise discard) |

> For each stuck session, you can choose to:
> * **Condense**: Save session data to permanent storage (`entire/checkpoints/v1` branch)
> * **Discard**: Remove the session state and shadow branch data
> * **Skip**: Leave the session as-is

Guide framing: "If status suggests a repository health issue, run: `entire doctor`."

Wrong-worktree fix:

```bash
entire session adopt SESSION_ID --from ../source-worktree
```

**Not documented:** no page states an automatic timeout that ends sessions on its own, nor any retention/GC policy for stale session state beyond `doctor`'s manual condense/discard.

## 5. Troubleshooting — symptom → cause → fix (verbatim from troubleshooting.md)

### No Active Session Appears
Check repository and hook status:
```bash
entire status
```
If Entire is not enabled, start with:
```bash
entire enable --agent AGENT
```
If Entire is already enabled but the agent is not configured, add it:
```bash
entire agent add AGENT
```
> Then start your agent from inside the enabled repository. Agent hooks only capture work for agents that are configured for that repo.

### The Session Did Not Link to a Commit
> A normal committed checkpoint needs both captured session context and a Git commit.

If the session exists but was not linked, attach it to the latest commit:
```bash
entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent AGENT
```
> If the commit already has a checkpoint, Entire adds the session to that checkpoint. Otherwise, Entire can create a new checkpoint and amend the commit with an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.

### The Session Is Attached to the Wrong Worktree
> If an agent started in one worktree and continued in another, adopt the session into the current repository:
```bash
entire session adopt SESSION_ID --from ../source-worktree
```
> After adoption, the next commit can link to the session normally.

### Stale Sessions Keep Showing Up
> Use `entire status` to find active and stale sessions. If a session is no longer running, stop it:
```bash
entire session stop SESSION_ID
```
For multiple stale sessions:
```bash
entire session stop --all
```
If status suggests a repository health issue, run:
```bash
entire doctor
```

### Token Usage Is Missing
> Token usage depends on what the agent exposes and when the session data is available. Some agents only expose full token usage after the session ends.

Check the session details first:
```bash
entire session info SESSION_ID
```
Then check token usage:
```bash
entire session tokens SESSION_ID
```

### The Raw Transcript Is Missing
> Entire reads transcript data from the agent's session storage. If the agent deleted or moved its local transcript, Entire may still have metadata but not the raw transcript bytes.

Try:
```bash
entire session info SESSION_ID --json
```
> If metadata exists but the transcript cannot be streamed, inspect the relevant agent guide (`/agents/overview`) for that agent's transcript requirements.

## 1. Session vs. Checkpoint, and lifecycle

### Session — definition (verbatim, overview.md)

> A session is the complete record of an AI coding interaction: the prompts, responses, tool calls, file changes, metadata, token usage, and checkpoint links Entire captured while the agent worked.

> Sessions show what the agent did, why it did it, and how the work came together.

**What sessions capture** (overview.md, verbatim list):
- prompts and agent responses
- tool calls, shell commands, file reads, and file edits
- files created, modified, or deleted during the session
- agent, model, worktree, timing, and token metadata
- checkpoints and commits linked to the session
- line attribution showing how much of a change came from the agent versus a human

### Checkpoint — definition `[REF glossary.md]`

> **Checkpoint**: A save point for your work. Entire creates checkpoints around agent activity and links committed checkpoints to Git commits.

> **Committed checkpoint**: A checkpoint permanently linked to a Git commit and stored on the checkpoints branch.

> **Checkpoint linking**: The connection between a Git commit and the Entire checkpoint that captured the session context behind it.

> **Session** (glossary): A complete interaction with an AI coding agent from start to finish. Sessions include prompts, responses, code changes, checkpoints, token usage, metadata, and line attribution.

### Session↔Checkpoint relationship (overview.md, table verbatim)

| Scenario | How it looks in Entire |
| --- | --- |
| One session, one checkpoint | Most common. You ask the agent to do something, it does the work, and you commit. |
| One checkpoint, multiple sessions | Several sessions contribute to the same change before you commit. |
| One session, multiple checkpoints | One longer session keeps going while you commit multiple checkpoints along the way. |
| Multiple sessions, multiple checkpoints | Multiple sessions and commits are linked across a larger or parallel piece of work. |

> Entire links these records so you can move from code, to checkpoint, to the session context behind it.

### How sessions are created (overview.md, verbatim)

> After you enable Entire for a repository, agent hooks capture session context while you work. When you commit, Entire can link the relevant session context to a checkpoint.

> You can also attach a session later if capture started late, hooks did not fire, or the session was useful even though it did not produce file changes.

Also, from troubleshooting.md: "A normal committed checkpoint needs both captured session context and a Git commit."

### ⚠️ Lifecycle — what the docs actually state vs. do not

**The docs do NOT publish a formal session state machine.** No page in the sessions guide enumerates a `start → active → end → checkpoint` transition list. Do not present one as documented. What *is* documented:

- Two named phases exist, but only in `[REF doctor.md]`: **`ACTIVE`** and **`ENDED`**.
- `entire session list` shows "sessions tracked by Entire, **including ended sessions**" (list-sessions.md), implying ended is a persisted terminal state.
- `entire session stop` "**marks sessions as ended**" (stop-sessions.md warning) — this is the only documented explicit transition, and it explicitly **does not** create a checkpoint.
- Resume operates on "**stopped sessions**" (resume-sessions.md) — "stopped" is used as a session state in the picker.
- Storage transition `[REF glossary.md + doctor.md]`: **Shadow branch** = "A temporary local branch used to store checkpoints during active sessions. Shadow branches are named like `entire/<sessionID>-<worktreeID>` and are not pushed to remote repositories." **Checkpoints branch** = "The permanent Git branch where Entire stores checkpoint and session metadata. The branch is named `entire/checkpoints/v1`." `doctor`'s **Condense** action moves data from the former to the latter.
- **Nested session** `[REF glossary.md]`: "A child session created when an agent spawns another agent or sub-agent during the same body of work." Behavior (sessions-in-entire-io.md): "When an agent spawns a sub-agent, Entire can capture that child session separately and roll its context into the parent checkpoint."
- **Agent run** `[REF glossary.md]`: "One execution of an agent inside a session." So a session can contain multiple runs.

## 2. Every session subcommand with exact flags

Base form `[REF sessions.md]`:

```bash
entire session SUBCOMMAND
```

> `entire session` is also available as `entire sessions`.

### `session current`
Show the most recently active session for the current worktree.

```bash
entire session current
entire session current --json
entire session current --transcript > session.jsonl
```

| Flag | Description `[REF]` |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Output as JSON |
| `--transcript` | Stream raw agent transcript bytes to stdout |

Guide notes: "the most relevant session for the current worktree" (list-sessions.md); "Transcript format depends on the agent." (inspect-sessions-in-cli.md)

### `session list`
List all sessions tracked by Entire, including ended sessions.

```bash
entire session list
entire session list --json
```

| Flag | Description `[REF]` |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Output as JSON |

`[REF]`: "For active sessions only, use `entire status`."

### `session info`

```bash
entire session info SESSION_ID
entire session info SESSION_ID --json
entire session info SESSION_ID --transcript > session.jsonl
```

| Flag | Description `[REF]` |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Output as JSON |
| `--transcript` | Stream raw agent transcript bytes to stdout |

Shows (both guide and REF, near-identical wording): "the agent, model, status, worktree, timing, token usage, checkpoint links, and files touched."

### `session tokens`

```bash
entire session tokens
entire session tokens SESSION_ID
entire session tokens --agent-brief
```

`[REF]` signature: `entire session tokens [SESSION_ID] [flags]` — "When no session ID is provided, Entire reports on the most recently active session for the current worktree."

| Flag | Description `[REF]` |
| --- | --- |
| `--agent-brief` | Output compact next-step guidance for agents |
| `--current` | Prefer the current worktree's most recent session |
| `--json` | Output as JSON |

Guide wording: "inspect token usage and optimization recommendations"; `--agent-brief` = "compact guidance that an agent can act on."

> `--current` and `--json` for `tokens` appear **only** in the CLI reference, not in the nine guide pages.

### `session stop`

```bash
entire status
entire session stop SESSION_ID
entire session stop --all
entire session stop --all --force
```

`[REF]` signature: `entire session stop [SESSION_ID] [flags]`

| Flag | Description `[REF]` |
| --- | --- |
| `--all` | Stop all active sessions |
| `-f, --force` | Skip confirmation prompt |

> **Warning (stop-sessions.md, verbatim):** `entire session stop` marks sessions as ended. It does not create a checkpoint or flush pending work. Commit first when you want session context linked to code changes.

### `session attach`

```bash
entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent AGENT
entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent AGENT --force
entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent codex --review
entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent codex --review --skills review
```

`[REF attach.md]` signature: `entire session attach SESSION_ID [flags]`

| Flag | Description `[REF]` |
| --- | --- |
| `-a, --agent NAME` | Agent that created the session. Defaults to `claude-code`. Run `entire agent list` to see registered agents, including external agents. |
| `-f, --force` | Skip confirmation and amend the last commit with the checkpoint trailer |
| `--review` | Tag the attached session as an agent review. |
| `--skills SKILL` | Declare which review skills were run. Repeatable; only used with `--review`. |

**When to attach** (attach-sessions.md, verbatim bullets):
- hooks were not installed when the session started
- hooks did not fire
- a research session should be linked to the latest commit
- a completed agent review should be preserved as review context

**Behavior:** "Attach reads an existing agent transcript, creates or updates a checkpoint, and links that context to the last commit. If the last commit already has an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, the session is added to that checkpoint. Otherwise, Entire creates a checkpoint and can amend the last commit with the trailer."

> **Note `[REF attach.md]`:** `entire session attach` requires the repository to already have at least one commit. If Entire cannot find the transcript for the agent you specify, it will try to auto-detect the correct agent from known transcript locations.

`[REF]` examples, verbatim:

```bash
# Attach a Codex session and amend HEAD automatically
entire session attach 019d6c43-1537-7343-9691-1f8cee04fe59 -a codex -f

# Attach a Claude Code session using the default agent
entire session attach 9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad-9bdd-2b0d7b3dcbfe

# Attach a Codex session as a review
entire session attach 019d6c43-1537-7343-9691-1f8cee04fe59 -a codex --review
```

### `session adopt`

Only appearance in the nine guides is troubleshooting.md:

```bash
entire session adopt SESSION_ID --from ../source-worktree
```

`[REF sessions.md]` signature: `entire session adopt [SESSION_ID] --from SOURCE_WORKTREE [flags]` — "Adopt an active session from another worktree into the current repository. Use this when an agent starts in one repository or worktree, then moves and makes changes in another."

| Flag | Description `[REF]` |
| --- | --- |
| `--from PATH` | Source worktree that already tracks the session |
| `--force` | Replace an existing local state file for the same session |
| `--yes` | Confirm same-store adoption and replacement without prompting |

Guide note: "After adoption, the next commit can link to the session normally."

### `session resume`

```bash
entire session resume
entire session resume BRANCH
entire session resume BRANCH --force
```

`[REF resume.md]` signature: `entire session resume [BRANCH] [flags]`

| Argument | Description `[REF]` |
| --- | --- |
| `branch` | Optional branch to resume the agent session from |

| Flag | Description `[REF]` |
| --- | --- |
| `-f, --force` | Resume from older checkpoint without confirmation |

**Picker mode (no argument):** "opens an interactive picker of stopped sessions across all worktrees. After you choose a session, Entire checks out the related branch, restores the session log if needed, and asks whether to start the agent."

**Branch mode — exact numbered steps `[REF resume.md]`:**
1. Checks out the specified branch
2. Finds the session ID from commits unique to this branch
3. Restores the session log if it does not exist locally
4. Shows or starts the command to resume the agent session

(Guide wording: "Entire finds the session ID from checkpoint-linked commits on that branch.")

> **Note `[REF]`:** If the branch doesn't exist locally but exists on origin, you'll be prompted to fetch it.

> **Warning (resume-sessions.md, verbatim):** If newer commits without checkpoints exist on the branch, resume can reset Git state to the most recent commit with a checkpoint. Entire prompts before doing this unless you force it.

> **Warning `[REF]`, fuller:** If newer commits without checkpoints exist on the branch (e.g., after merging main or cherry-picking), this operation will reset your Git status to the most recent commit with a checkpoint. You'll be prompted to confirm.

### Finding a session ID (list-sessions.md)

```bash
entire session info SESSION_ID
entire session stop SESSION_ID
entire session tokens SESSION_ID
```

> Use `entire status`, `entire session current`, or `entire session list` when you need to copy that ID.

## 3. Importing past agent history (predating Entire)

Command family is **`entire import AGENT`** — not a `session` subcommand.

**When to use** (import-past-agent-history.md, verbatim bullets):
- you enabled Entire after useful agent work already happened
- you want past local agent sessions to become searchable in Entire
- you want to import sessions from an agent's local transcript store

| If you want to | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Bring past local agent sessions into Entire | `entire import AGENT` |
| Link one missed session to the latest commit | `entire session attach` |
| Continue working from an earlier session | `entire session resume` |

### Commands

```bash
entire import claude-code --dry-run
entire import claude-code
entire import claude-code --session SESSION_ID
entire import claude-code --path TRANSCRIPT_DIRECTORY
```

- Run import **from inside the repository** whose agent history you want to bring in.
- Replace `claude-code` with the agent you want to import from.
- `--dry-run` preview "shows how many sessions and turns Entire found, what would be imported, and what was already imported."
- "You can repeat `--session` to import more than one session."
- "Run `entire import --help` or see the import command reference for supported agents and flags."

| Flag `[REF import.md]` | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Report what would be imported without writing checkpoints |
| `--path DIRECTORY` | Override the transcript directory to import from |
| `--session ID` | Import only this session ID. Repeatable. |

### Supported agents `[REF import.md]` — "In Entire CLI `0.7.8`, import supports:"

| Agent | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `entire import claude-code` |
| Codex | `entire import codex` |
| Copilot CLI | `entire import copilot-cli` |
| Cursor | `entire import cursor` |
| Factory | `entire import factoryai-droid` |
| Gemini CLI | `entire import gemini` |
| Pi | `entire import pi` |

### Limits — the critical ones

**⚠️ Time window (only stated in `[REF import.md]`, NOT in the guide page):**

> `entire import` scans the agent's local transcript store for the current repository and imports **history from the past month**.

**⚠️ Experimental status `[REF import.md]`:**

> `entire import` is experimental and hidden from the top-level help in Entire CLI `0.7.8`. Run `entire import --help` to see the agents supported by your installed CLI version.

**Imported checkpoints are (guide page, verbatim):**
- searchable
- explainable
- idempotent, so re-running import skips turns that already exist
- **not linked to a Git commit**
- **not rewindable**

Plus: "Imported sessions are stored as read-only checkpoints on Entire's checkpoint metadata branch." `[REF]` adds **read-only** as an explicit first bullet.

## 4. Stuck / orphaned sessions

**Terminology caveat:** the docs never use the word "orphaned." The nine guides use "**stale**"; the CLI reference uses "**stuck**." Treat them as the documented vocabulary.

### How they happen
- Guides state only the situational cause: "Stop a session when Entire still considers it active, but the agent run is finished or no longer relevant." (stop-sessions.md)
- Wrong-worktree case: "If an agent started in one worktree and continued in another…" (troubleshooting.md)

### Detection — exact criteria `[REF doctor.md]`

> A session is considered stuck if:
> * It is in ACTIVE phase with no interaction for over 1 hour
> * It is in ENDED phase with uncondensed checkpoint data on a shadow branch

Detection commands:

```bash
entire status          # find active and stale sessions
entire doctor          # scan for stuck sessions and offer fixes
```

### Clearing

```bash
entire session stop SESSION_ID
entire session stop --all
entire session stop --all --force
entire doctor
```

`entire doctor` flags and choices `[REF doctor.md]`:

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-f, --force` | Fix all issues without prompting (condense if possible, otherwise discard) |

> For each stuck session, you can choose to:
> * **Condense**: Save session data to permanent storage (`entire/checkpoints/v1` branch)
> * **Discard**: Remove the session state and shadow branch data
> * **Skip**: Leave the session as-is

Guide framing: "If status suggests a repository health issue, run: `entire doctor`."

Wrong-worktree fix:

```bash
entire session adopt SESSION_ID --from ../source-worktree
```

**Not documented:** no page states an automatic timeout that ends sessions on its own, nor any retention/GC policy for stale session state beyond `doctor`'s manual condense/discard.

## 5. Troubleshooting — symptom → cause → fix (verbatim from troubleshooting.md)

### No Active Session Appears
Check repository and hook status:
```bash
entire status
```
If Entire is not enabled, start with:
```bash
entire enable --agent AGENT
```
If Entire is already enabled but the agent is not configured, add it:
```bash
entire agent add AGENT
```
> Then start your agent from inside the enabled repository. Agent hooks only capture work for agents that are configured for that repo.

### The Session Did Not Link to a Commit
> A normal committed checkpoint needs both captured session context and a Git commit.

If the session exists but was not linked, attach it to the latest commit:
```bash
entire session attach SESSION_ID --agent AGENT
```
> If the commit already has a checkpoint, Entire adds the session to that checkpoint. Otherwise, Entire can create a new checkpoint and amend the commit with an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.

### The Session Is Attached to the Wrong Worktree
> If an agent started in one worktree and continued in another, adopt the session into the current repository:
```bash
entire session adopt SESSION_ID --from ../source-worktree
```
> After adoption, the next commit can link to the session normally.

### Stale Sessions Keep Showing Up
> Use `entire status` to find active and stale sessions. If a session is no longer running, stop it:
```bash
entire session stop SESSION_ID
```
For multiple stale sessions:
```bash
entire session stop --all
```
If status suggests a repository health issue, run:
```bash
entire doctor
```

### Token Usage Is Missing
> Token usage depends on what the agent exposes and when the session data is available. Some agents only expose full token usage after the session ends.

Check the session details first:
```bash
entire session info SESSION_ID
```
Then check token usage:
```bash
entire session tokens SESSION_ID
```

### The Raw Transcript Is Missing
> Entire reads transcript data from the agent's session storage. If the agent deleted or moved its local transcript, Entire may still have metadata but not the raw transcript bytes.

Try:
```bash
entire session info SESSION_ID --json
```
> If metadata exists but the transcript cannot be streamed, inspect the relevant agent guide (`/agents/overview`) for that agent's transcript requirements.
